title: Sep 22 Results + Sep 23 Preview: 60% Isn't Pretty, But It's a Win
summary: 9-6 on Sep 22 with some ugly misses. Tomorrow we're riding Framber and the Tigers.

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: Today Was Messy

Look, 60% accuracy sounds decent on paper, but let's not pretend this was some masterclass performance. We went 9-6 on Sep 22, and while that's technically a winning day, half those picks felt like coin flips that happened to land our way. The Rangers pick at 50%? That was basically throwing darts blindfolded. And don't even get me started on the Cubs debacle.

## The Brutal Truth About Today's Picks

Six losses. SIX. And you know what the worst part is? Three of those losses came from picks where we had 60%+ confidence. The Tigers let us down at 62%, the Cubs embarrassed us at 61%, and the Braves couldn't deliver at 51%. When your high-confidence picks fail, that's not bad luck—that's a reality check.

The Rays split their doubleheader exactly how you'd expect chaos to unfold, and somehow we only got one right. The Mets-Rangers pick? We chose Texas at 50-50 odds. That's not analysis, that's a guess with a fancy percentage attached to it.

## The Silver Lining Nobody Asked For

Here's the thing: we still finished above .500, and in baseball betting, that's literally all that matters. You don't get style points for picking pretty games. The Guardians, Pirates, and Sox picks came through when we needed them, even if the confidence levels were basically shrugs.

But let's not pop champagne. A 60% day is pedestrian. It's a C+ on a good grading curve. We should be hitting 65-70% on these slates if the model is actually worth trusting.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Time to Get Serious

Sep 23 brings us back to a game we already failed at yesterday—Nationals versus Tigers. And you know what? I'm not even mad we're going back to this well. Sometimes you need to learn from your mistakes, and sometimes the matchup is just too good to ignore.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 23 Top Pick
content.sub: 61% win probability · Framber Valdez vs Richard Lovelady

content.value:
## Why the Tigers Will Actually Show Up This Time

Let me be brutally honest: picking the Tigers again after they burned us yesterday takes either courage or stupidity. I'm betting on courage. Here's why:

**Framber Valdez is on the mound.** If you don't know that name, you haven't been paying attention. This is a legitimate ace who can dominate any lineup, especially one as anemic as Washington's. The Nationals are sending out Richard Lovelady, and while that's a great name for a romance novel protagonist, it's a terrible sign for their win probability.

The Tigers are at home, they're fighting for something, and they've got the pitching advantage that actually matters. Yesterday's loss? That was the exception. Tomorrow is the rule.

## The Hot Take You Didn't Ask For

If the Tigers lose again tomorrow with Valdez on the mound against THIS Nationals roster, we're not just questioning the model—we're questioning if Detroit even wants to win games. But they will. 61% feels almost conservative.

Sep 22 was messy. Sep 23 is redemption day. Let's ride.

author: Rico
